literature.headline_zh: 埃博拉病毒类群本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期埃博拉病毒类群研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 重组 BDBV-ZsG 表现出与野生型 BDBV 亲本毒株相当的抑制特性,并在单克隆抗体和恢复期血清样品的中和测定中显示出强大的灵敏度和特异性。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2709847]
历史病死率已从 1970 年代的约 65% 下降至最近的 暴发 的约 50%,预计较 疫苗 的影响减少 15%;然而,目前还没有获得许可的 疫苗 或针对本迪布焦埃博拉病毒的靶向治疗药物。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10092649/v1]
比较分析确定了分布在整个 GP 序列中的 21 个核心氨基酸取代位点。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10265918/v1]
菌血症在 CCHF 患者中最常见 (n = 46),其次是 EVD (n = 16)、MVD (n = 16) 和 LF (n = 2)。在非洲以外地区接受治疗的 27 名埃博拉病毒病患者中,有 7 名 (26%) 患有细菌合并感染。在 HCVI 中,菌血症在症状出现后的中位时间(范围 0-23)检测到 11 天,并且与败血症的特征相关。 [10.1093/ofid/ofag404]
埃博拉病毒感染引发巨噬细胞转录组的广泛重塑;LINC01740 被强烈诱导并与 ATF3 紧密共表达,LINC01740 敲除降低了 ATF3 表达,而 ATF3 抑制则恢复了干扰素 β 的产生并增强了 抗病毒药物 反应。 [10.1093/jimmun/vkag141.818]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The recombinant BDBV-ZsG demonstrated comparable inhibitory profiles to the wild-type BDBV parental strain and showed robust sensitivity and specificity in neutralization assays with monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2709847]

Historical case fatality rates have declined from approximately 65% in the 1970s to around 50% in recent outbreaks, with an estimated 15% reduction from vaccine impact; however, no licensed vaccines or targeted therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo ebolavirus. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10092649/v1]
Comparative analysis identified 21 core amino acid substitution sites distributed throughout the GP sequence. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10265918/v1]

Bacteremia was most commonly reported among patients with CCHF (n = 46), followed by EVD (n = 16), MVD (n = 16), and LF (n = 2). Of 27 EVD patients treated outside Africa, seven (26%) had bacterial coinfection. [10.1093/ofid/ofag404]

EBOV infection triggered extensive remodeling of the macrophage transcriptome; LINC01740 was strongly induced and tightly co-expressed with ATF3, and LINC01740 knockdown reduced ATF3 expression while ATF3 inhibition restored interferon-beta production and enhanced antiviral responses. [10.1093/jimmun/vkag141.818]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期埃博拉病毒类群研究集中呈现以下进展。

历史病死率已从 1970 年代的约 65% 下降至最近的 暴发 的约 50%,预计较 疫苗 的影响减少 15%;然而,目前还没有获得许可的 疫苗 或针对本迪布焦埃博拉病毒的靶向治疗药物。
比较分析确定了分布在整个 GP 序列中的 21 个核心氨基酸取代位点。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10265918/v1]。
菌血症在 CCHF 患者中最常见 (n = 46),其次是 EVD (n = 16)、MVD (n = 16) 和 LF (n = 2)。在非洲以外地区接受治疗的 27 名埃博拉病毒病患者中,有 7 名 (26%) 患有细菌合并感染。在 HCVI 中,菌血症在症状出现后的中位时间(范围 0-23)检测到 11 天,并且与败血症的特征相关。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

The recombinant BDBV-ZsG demonstrated comparable inhibitory profiles to the wild-type BDBV parental strain and showed robust sensitivity and specificity in neutralization assays with monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.

Historical case fatality rates have declined from approximately 65% in the 1970s to around 50% in recent outbreaks, with an estimated 15% reduction from vaccine impact; however, no licensed vaccines or targeted therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo ebolavirus.

Comparative analysis identified 21 core amino acid substitution sites distributed throughout the GP sequence. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10265918/v1]. Bacteremia was most commonly reported among patients with CCHF (n = 46), followed by EVD (n = 16), MVD (n = 16), and LF (n = 2). Of 27 EVD patients treated outside Africa, seven (26%) had bacterial coinfection.

papers.title: Development and Characterization of a Recombinant Bundibugyo Virus Expressing a Fluorescent Reporter Protein.
papers.abstract: Abstract Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with previous outbreaks reporting case fatality rates of 30%-50%. The ongoing BDBV outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda highlights the urgent need for virus-specific research tools and medical countermeasures. Unlike Ebola virus disease caused by Zaire ebolavirus, no licensed vaccines or specific therapeutics are currently available for BVD. The lack of research tools has limited studies with BDBV. To facilitate antiviral testing and neutralization studies, we developed the first recombinant BDBV expressing the fluorescent reporter protein ZsGreen (rBDBV-ZsG). As a proof of concept, we tested a set of previously characterized antiviral compounds and demonstrated comparable inhibitory profiles between rBDBV-ZsG and the wild-type BDBV parental strain. Furthermore, the utility of rBDBV-ZsG was successfully evaluated in neutralization assays, demonstrating robust sensitivity and specificity using monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) causes substantial morbidity and mortality with case fatality rates of 30%-50%, and the ongoing outbreak highlights the urgent need for virus-specific research tools and medical countermeasures, as no licensed vaccines or specific therapeutics are currently available for BVD.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed the first recombinant Bundibugyo virus expressing the fluorescent reporter protein ZsGreen (rBDBV-ZsG) to facilitate antiviral testing and neutralization studies.
analysis.methods: The recombinant virus was tested with previously characterized antiviral compounds to compare inhibitory profiles with the wild-type BDBV parental strain, and its utility was evaluated in neutralization assays using monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.
analysis.main_results: The recombinant BDBV-ZsG demonstrated comparable inhibitory profiles to the wild-type BDBV parental strain and showed robust sensitivity and specificity in neutralization assays with monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The development of rBDBV-ZsG provides a valuable tool for antiviral testing and neutralization studies, addressing the previous limitation of lacking research tools for BDBV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The recombinant virus can accelerate the development of medical countermeasures for BVD by enabling efficient screening of antiviral compounds and evaluation of immune responses.

papers.title_zh: 表达荧光报告蛋白的重组 Bundibugyo 病毒的开发和表征。
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with previous outbreaks reporting case fatality rates of 30%-50%. The ongoing BDBV outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda highlights the urgent need for virus-specific research tools and medical countermeasures. Unlike Ebola virus disease caused by Zaire ebolavirus, no licensed vaccines or specific therapeutics are currently available for BVD. The lack of research tools has limited studies with BDBV. To facilitate antiviral testing and neutralization studies, we developed the first recombinant BDBV expressing the fluorescent reporter protein ZsGreen (rBDBV-ZsG). As a proof of concept, we tested a set of previously characterized antiviral compounds and demonstrated comparable inhibitory profiles between rBDBV-ZsG and the wild-type BDBV parental strain. Furthermore, the utility of rBDBV-ZsG was successfully evaluated in neutralization assays, demonstrating robust sensitivity and specificity using monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.

papers.title: Bacterial infection in Ebola virus disease, Marburg virus disease, Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever, and Lassa fever
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Concern for bacterial coinfection in patients with high consequence viral infections (HCVIs) has made the empiric antibiotic administration the standard of care. However, the incidence, microbiology, and clinical significance of bacterial coinfection in HCVIs remain unclear. Methods We conducted a systematic review of case reports, cohort studies, and cross-sectional analyses describing bacterial coinfection in Ebola virus disease (EVD), Marburg virus disease (MVD), Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF), and Lassa fever (LF). Data were extracted on study design, setting, diagnostic methods, pathogens, antibiotic use, and outcomes. Results Thirty publications met inclusion criteria. Bacteremia was most commonly reported among patients with CCHF (n = 46), followed by EVD (n = 16), MVD (n = 16), and LF (n = 2). Of 27 EVD patients treated outside Africa, seven (26%) had bacterial coinfection. Across HCVIs, bacteremia was detected a median of 11 days after symptom onset (range 0–23) and was associated with features of sepsis. Pathogens included enteric flora, healthcare-associated organisms, opportunistic pathogens, and zoonotic bacteria—most notably Brucella spp. Ceftriaxone was the most common empiric antibiotic but is predicted to have activity against a minority of bloodstream isolates. Mortality among coinfected patients with EVD or MVD was similar to those without bacterial coinfection, whereas coinfected CCHF patients had higher mortality than those without coinfection (15.5%; 95% CI 8.0–25.9% vs 5.7%; 95% CI 5.1–6.4%). Conclusions Despite being a major concern driving empiric antibiotic use, bacterial coinfection in HCVIs remains poorly described, precluding determination of its incidence or clinical significance. Prospective studies with standardized protocols for bacterial diagnosis and characterization of antimicrobial resistance are needed to guide antimicrobial strategies.

papers.title: Vaccine gaps in Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak control and their implications for global public health preparedness and response
papers.abstract: Abstract The present study aims to critically examine recurrent Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreaks—particularly Bundibugyo ebolavirus—with a focus on epidemiological trends, and gaps in vaccinology and public health preparedness, in order to inform concerted outbreak response and global health security strategies. Historical trends show a gradual decline in overall case fatality rates from approximately 65% in the 1970s to around 50% in recent outbreaks, reflecting improvements in clinical care, surveillance, and response systems and potential vaccine impact with estimated approximately 15% impact in CFR reduction from the ITS analysis. However, substantial disparities remain between high-income and low-resource settings. The current epidemic exposes a critical gap in biomedical preparedness, as no licensed vaccines or targeted therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo ebolavirus, unlike Zaire ebolavirus. Hence, outbreak control continues to rely heavily on non-pharmaceutical interventions, including case detection, isolation, contact tracing, and community engagement. Ongoing transmission is exacerbated by conflict, population displacement, and weak health infrastructure. Strengthening preparedness will require sustained global investment in vaccine development, improved surveillance at human–animal interfaces and coordinated international research and response frameworks.

source_records.abstract: Abstract The present study aims to critically examine recurrent Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreaks—particularly Bundibugyo ebolavirus—with a focus on epidemiological trends, and gaps in vaccinology and public health preparedness, in order to inform concerted outbreak response and global health security strategies. Historical trends show a gradual decline in overall case fatality rates from approximately 65% in the 1970s to around 50% in recent outbreaks, reflecting improvements in clinical care, surveillance, and response systems and potential vaccine impact with estimated approximately 15% impact in CFR reduction from the ITS analysis. However, substantial disparities remain between high-income and low-resource settings. The current epidemic exposes a critical gap in biomedical preparedness, as no licensed vaccines or targeted therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo ebolavirus, unlike Zaire ebolavirus. Hence, outbreak control continues to rely heavily on non-pharmaceutical interventions, including case detection, isolation, contact tracing, and community engagement. Ongoing transmission is exacerbated by conflict, population displacement, and weak health infrastructure. Strengthening preparedness will require sustained global investment in vaccine development, improved surveillance at human–animal interfaces and coordinated international research and response frameworks.

analysis.methods: The study employs an interrupted time series analysis to estimate the impact of vaccines on case fatality rates and examines the current epidemic's biomedical preparedness gaps, particularly for Bundibugyo ebolavirus.

papers.full_text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which had been circulating undetected for months. The response is now catching up across a region weakened by conflict, displacement and loss of humanitarian aid. With no licensed vaccine or treatment, containment will depend on rebuilding resources, access and trust in public health systems. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and its neighbouring countries face an incredible challenge in the new Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) disease outbreak. By the time the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in Kinshasa confirmed BDBV in Ituri Province, officials had already recorded 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths across several health zones. Confirmed cases were soon logged across multiple DRC provinces and in Kampala, the capital of neighbouring Uganda1. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May, and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention followed with a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 18 May, naming ten other countries at high risk of spread2,3. The scale of those initial figures made it evident that the world was not discovering a new outbreak so much as uncovering one that had been silently circulating, hidden by the fragility of local healthcare capacity and propagated by conflict, community distrust and population mobility. As of 31 May, 336 cases had been confirmed across both countries, with 49 confirmed deaths, alongside 220 suspected cases and 236 suspected deaths in the DRC. These numbers are almost certainly an undercount. A modelling group at Imperial College London estimated within days of the declaration that true infections probably already exceeded 900, and many community deaths have never entered a formal record4. Unlike West Africa in 2013, where the index case seeded a region with no prior filovirus experience, the DRC and its neighbours have extensive experience with viral haemorrhagic fevers, including 10 outbreaks in the past 5 years alone. The communities and health workers of the region have shown remarkable resilience across these repeated emergencies, carrying the burden of response, often at great personal cost, with limited and intermittent external support. However, a confluence of factors is lining up to make this outbreak at least the second-biggest Ebola crisis the world has seen. First, delayed laboratory identification allowed geographic expansion, and the response is now playing catch-up. The initial delay followed negative Ebola testing at the provincial laboratory in Bunia, which required specimens to be sent to Kinshasa for species-specific confirmation. Even before the 5 May alert to the WHO, some unexplained illnesses had been noted in the region with negative testing for common pathogens, highlighting regional blind spots leading to the current crisis, which may have resulted from sudden withdrawal of aid. The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was historically the DRC’s largest humanitarian donor and since its dissolution the DRC has seen surge in cholera, mpox and measles across its eastern provinces, conditions under which an uncommon disease is far harder to distinguish from the common ones5. Although most cases remain in Ituri, patients have been confirmed hundreds of kilometres away in North and South Kivu Provinces, in eastern DRC. These multiple fronts require already-strained resources — treatment units, infection prevention and sanitation supplies, contact tracers, laboratory capacity and community engagement — to be divided even further. Financial commitments have been made by the national government and the global community, but there is typically a lag between the appropriation of funds and their conversion into contracts, procurement and distribution, making this the most precarious moment of the response. Reports from affected areas indicate that personal protective equipment and diagnostic supplies are severely lagging behind need6. Active conflict is impeding access, and that conflict has worsened with the withdrawal of aid that followed the dismantling of USAID. On 28 May, the WHO Director-General travelled to the DRC to appeal for a ceasefire, enabling central outbreak control efforts to continue: bringing sick patients into isolation, assuring them they will be safe as they receive care, and tracing their contacts across an insecure terrain. In this outbreak, trust is as valuable and critical as monetary funds. A population-based survey during the 2018–2019 North Kivu outbreak found that only about a third of respondents trusted that local authorities represented their interests, and a quarter believed the outbreak was not real7. During that outbreak, the WHO recorded roughly 390 attacks on health facilities and workers in 2019 (ref. 8). The same dynamics are now compounded by displacement and the loss of the previously funded community programmes. Because there have been only two previous outbreaks, research on BDBV medical countermeasures lags between that for Zaire and Sudan ebolaviruses, for which there are either approved products or more products with safety and efficacy data. Although arrangements for vaccine and therapeutic trials are underway, the manufacturing and trial timelines mean deployment is likely to be months away9. Their capacity to alter the trajectory of this outbreak, at least in the near term, is therefore limited. And that trajectory is concerning. The outbreak will probably continue for months, potentially into 2027, with a high risk of spread into areas hosting displaced and refugee populations and across borders, making regional collaboration essential. Although BDBV is unlikely to cause a pandemic, as cases rise, sporadic suspect cases may surface in travellers worldwide, particularly given the nonspecific early symptoms of Ebola. Despite the alarm these cases generate, the base rate of true infection among travellers is very low, and the overwhelming majority of suspected cases evaluated elsewhere will test negative. BDBV mortality has ranged from 30% to 50% in the historical record, lower than the roughly 40–66% seen in large Zaire ebolavirus outbreaks. But those estimates rest on a small number of patients, and case fatality rates shift over the arc of an outbreak. Early mortality may be high, reflecting delays in reaching care and a shortage of treatment resources. As more resources arrive, a falling case fatality rate would indicate two improvements at once: better success in building trust and bringing patients in, and better supportive care once they arrive. The current numbers could be read as a measure of the response’s reach as well as the virus’s lethality. Lastly, the current outbreak is occurring in the middle of another underlying shift: US global aid architecture is shifting towards new approaches, such as ‘America First’ bilateral agreements, rather than investment in multilateral and sector-wide health programmes. African countries are re-examining how regional commitments can be consolidated to build a safer, more self-reliant future10. The containment of Bundibugyo virus outbreak, and the inevitable outbreaks that will follow it, will require consistent commitment on both fronts at once: regional investment that builds standing capacity where these viruses emerge, and global solidarity that is durable rather than episodic. A reactive posture, in which funding is surged only after a crisis has occurred, leaves us backfooted, particularly in areas of complex humanitarian emergencies. This creates massive gaps in timely resources, the cost of which is paid in patient lives and healthcare worker safety. References - World Health Organization. A modelling group at Imperial College London estimated within days of the declaration that true infections probably already exceeded 900, and many community deaths have never entered a formal record4. Unlike West Africa in 2013, where the index case seeded a region with no prior filovirus experience, the DRC and its neighbours have extensive experience with viral haemorrhagic fevers, including 10 outbreaks in the past 5 years alone. The communities and health workers of the region have shown remarkable resilience across these repeated emergencies, carrying the burden of response, often at great personal cost, with limited and intermittent external support. However, a confluence of factors is lining up to make this outbreak at least the second-biggest Ebola crisis the world has seen. First, delayed laboratory identification allowed geographic expansion, and the response is now playing catch-up. The initial delay followed negative Ebola testing at the provincial laboratory in Bunia, which required specimens to be sent to Kinshasa for species-specific confirmation. Even before the 5 May alert to the WHO, some unexplained illnesses had been noted in the region with negative testing for common pathogens, highlighting regional blind spots leading to the current crisis, which may have resulted from sudden withdrawal of aid. The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was historically the DRC’s largest humanitarian donor and since its dissolution the DRC has seen surge in cholera, mpox and measles across its eastern provinces, conditions under which an uncommon disease is far harder to distinguish from the common ones5. Although most cases remain in Ituri, patients have been confirmed hundreds of kilometres away in North and South Kivu Provinces, in eastern DRC. These multiple fronts require already-strained resources — treatment units, infection prevention and sanitation supplies, contact tracers, laboratory capacity and community engagement — to be divided even further. Financial commitments have been made by the national government and the global community, but there is typically a lag between the appropriation of funds and their conversion into contracts, procurement and distribution, making this the most precarious moment of the response. Reports from affected areas indicate that personal protective equipment and diagnostic supplies are severely lagging behind need6. Active conflict is impeding access, and that conflict has worsened with the withdrawal of aid that followed the dismantling of USAID. On 28 May, the WHO Director-General travelled to the DRC to appeal for a ceasefire, enabling central outbreak control efforts to continue: bringing sick patients into isolation, assuring them they will be safe as they receive care, and tracing their contacts across an insecure terrain. In this outbreak, trust is as valuable and critical as monetary funds. A population-based survey during the 2018–2019 North Kivu outbreak found that only about a third of respondents trusted that local authorities represented their interests, and a quarter believed the outbreak was not real7. During that outbreak, the WHO recorded roughly 390 attacks on health facilities and workers in 2019 (ref. 8). The same dynamics are now compounded by displacement and the loss of the previously funded community programmes. Because there have been only two previous outbreaks, research on BDBV medical countermeasures lags between that for Zaire and Sudan ebolaviruses, for which there are either approved products or more products with safety and efficacy data. Although arrangements for vaccine and therapeutic trials are underway, the manufacturing and trial timelines mean deployment is likely to be months away9. Their capacity to alter the trajectory of this outbreak, at least in the near term, is therefore limited. And that trajectory is concerning. The outbreak will probably continue for months, potentially into 2027, with a high risk of spread into areas hosting displaced and refugee populations and across borders, making regional collaboration essential. Although BDBV is unlikely to cause a pandemic, as cases rise, sporadic suspect cases may surface in travellers worldwide, particularly given the nonspecific early symptoms of Ebola. Despite the alarm these cases generate, the base rate of true infection among travellers is very low, and the overwhelming majority of suspected cases evaluated elsewhere will test negative. BDBV mortality has ranged from 30% to 50% in the historical record, lower than the roughly 40–66% seen in large Zaire ebolavirus outbreaks. But those estimates rest on a small number of patients, and case fatality rates shift over the arc of an outbreak. Early mortality may be high, reflecting delays in reaching care and a shortage of treatment resources. As more resources arrive, a falling case fatality rate would indicate two improvements at once: better success in building trust and bringing patients in, and better supportive care once they arrive. The current numbers could be read as a measure of the response’s reach as well as the virus’s lethality. Lastly, the current outbreak is occurring in the middle of another underlying shift: US global aid architecture is shifting towards new approaches, such as ‘America First’ bilateral agreements, rather than investment in multilateral and sector-wide health programmes. African countries are re-examining how regional commitments can be consolidated to build a safer, more self-reliant future10. The containment of Bundibugyo virus outbreak, and the inevitable outbreaks that will follow it, will require consistent commitment on both fronts at once: regional investment that builds standing capacity where these viruses emerge, and global solidarity that is durable rather than episodic. A reactive posture, in which funding is surged only after a crisis has occurred, leaves us backfooted, particularly in areas of complex humanitarian emergencies. This creates massive gaps in timely resources, the cost of which is paid in patient lives and healthcare worker safety. References - World Health Organization. analysis.summary_en: The Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries has become a major public health crisis, with 336 confirmed cases and 49 deaths as of 31 May. The outbreak was exacerbated by delayed laboratory identification, regional healthcare fragility, and factors like conflict and population mobility. With no licensed vaccine or treatment, containment depends on rebuilding public health resources and trust. The scale of the outbreak, likely underestimated, highlights the need for improved surveillance and response in regions with repeated emergencies.

papers.full_text: nature microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-026-02432-1 News & views Viral infection Ebola virus persistence and the hidden cost of immune privilege Amal Fahmi, Isabel Schultz-Pernice & Marco P. Alves Human brain organoids reveal how Ebola virus establishes persistent infection within the immune-privileged environment of the central nervous system. The idea of immune privilege has reshaped our understanding of how the immune system is regulated across tissues. It is viewed as a state of selective immune tolerance characterized by tissue- and organ-specific immune regulation. Classic examples include the central nervous sys- tem (CNS), eyes and testes, where immune surveillance is present but constrained. These sites maintain a highly regulated immunological milieu through cellular barriers, local immunoregulatory mediators and context-dependent modulation of antigen presentation. While this restrained inflammatory tone is essential to preserve the function and integrity of indispensable tissues, it comes at a cost: the same features that limit immunopathology can also reduce pathogen clearance. As a result, immune-privileged niches may be co-opted by pathogens as long-term reservoirs and enable persistence despite systemic immune surveillance. Understanding how viruses exploit these specialized envi- ronments is therefore critical for defining the mechanisms underlying chronic infection and relapse. Numerous studies have characterized viral replication dynamics, transmission and evolution during acute Ebola virus (EBOV) infection. However, increasing evidence indicates that EBOV can persist during the chronic phase, with ongoing viral replication in survivors sup- porting the concept that persistence represents an active infection Check for updates Immune-privileged CNS • Restrained inflammation • Cellular barriers (for example, BBB and choroid plexus) • Antigen drainage (glymphatics and meningeal lymphatics) • Limited immune surveillance EBOV persistence in the brain Virus exploits immune privilege to establish long-term infection The hidden cost Chronic neuroinflammation Type I IFNs and inflammatory mediators Neuron Astrocyte Microglia Oligodendrocyte Defective viral genomes Viral evolution Persistent reservoirs Neuronal dysfunction and injury Fig. 1 | Immune privilege as a double-edged sword during EBOV persistence in the CNS. The CNS maintains a tightly regulated immune environment that limits inflammation and preserves tissue integrity. In human brain organoids, EBOV infects multiple neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia, via viral spread through budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission. Persistent infection is associated with viral evolution and accumulation of defective viral genomes, mechanisms thought to favour chronic low-level replication. In parallel, activated microglia produce pro- inflammatory mediators and type I interferons (IFNs) that may drive chronic neuroinflammation and neuronal injury. BBB, blood–brain barrier. nature microbiology News & views within immune-privileged reservoirs1. Among these niches, the CNS has emerged as a particularly clinically relevant site, as studies in non- human primates have demonstrated that replication-competent EBOV can remain in the brain after clearance from the periphery, leading to fatal relapses2. Yet the mechanisms underlying EBOV persistence in the human CNS remain poorly understood, leaving key questions unanswered regarding the neural cell populations that support long- term infection and the associated host responses. In this issue of Nature Microbiology, Widerspick and colleagues3 provide mechanistic insights on how orthoebolaviruses exploit the CNS’s immune-privileged status to establish long-term persistence. The authors developed a human brain organoid model that enables long-term analysis of orthoebolavirus infection in the human neural tissue and tested EBOV (species Orthoebolavirus zairense), Sudan virus (species Orthoebolavirus sudanense), Reston virus (species Orthoe- bolavirus restonense), and a related filovirus, Marburg virus (species Orthomarburgvirus marburgense). In these organoids, they show that EBOV can persist for up to 120 days within diverse neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, microglia and oligodendrocytes. This persistence, referring to the continued presence of infectious virus or viral genetic material beyond the acute phase of infection, suggests that EBOV can establish a sustained reservoir within human neural tissue. Mechanistically, the study shows that EBOV persistence relies on both canonical viral budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission through actin-dependent cellular projections and syncytia formation. Cell-to- cell spread is recognized as a potential mechanism of immune evasion, allowing viruses to disseminate while potentially reducing exposure to soluble immune mediators4. Within highly interconnected neural tissue, this mode of spread may be advantageous, as shown by our recent work demonstrating that monkeypox virus exploits neuronal connectivity to propagate while limiting immune exposure5. Widerspick and colleagues observed that long-term persistence of EBOV was associated with ongoing viral evolution together with the accumulation of defective viral genomes. Defective viral genomes are increasingly recognized as regulators of persistent infection because they can attenuate cytopathic replication while allowing for minimal levels of viral activity. By interfering with replication of full-length viral genomes, defective viral genomes have been proposed to modulate viral replication and host responses, potentially reducing cytopathic effects and contributing to persistence6. Importantly, the study iden- tifies marked cell type-specific differences in the host response to persistent EBOV infection. Whereas infected astrocytes remained comparatively quiescent, microglia mounted robust pro-inflammatory and type I interferon responses, identifying these cells as likely drivers of the chronic neuroinflammation associated with EBOV persistence. This observation reinforces the concept that immune privilege may support long-term viral maintenance while allowing inflammatory responses to emerge once local immune activation is engaged (Fig. 1). Similar patterns have been observed in other neurotropic viral infections. Replication-competent Zika virus, for example, can persist in the brains of surviving mice for more than 1 year within inflamma- tory foci enriched in activated microglia and astrocytes, where viral persistence is associated with chronic inflammation and neuronal injury7. More broadly, persistent viral reservoirs represent one of sev- eral proposed mechanisms contributing to post-acute sequelae of infection, including long COVID, in which sustained immune activation may result from a combination of viral persistence, immune dysregula- tion and other host factors8,9. Whether the mechanisms of CNS persis- tence identified for EBOV are conserved among other Orthoebolavirus species such as Bundibugyo virus — the driving pathogen of the current Ebola disease outbreak — remains unclear. Bundibugyo virus has shown evidence of CNS involvement in animal models, with viral antigen and RNA detected in CNS-associated tissues10,11, and long-term neurological sequelae reported in human survivors12. However, whether Bundibugyo virus establishes CNS persistence through similar cellular tropism and host–virus interactions remains unknown. Comparative studies will be required to determine whether CNS persistence represents a conserved feature across all orthoebolaviruses and to define the viral and host determinants that enable long-term infection within neural tissue. Although brain organoids provide a valuable platform to investi- gate EBOV persistence in human neural tissue, they remain a simplified representation of the CNS and do not fully recapitulate the complex immune, barrier and cellular interactions that shape viral persistence within the intact CNS. Consequently, caution is warranted when extrapo- lating these findings to human disease. This is particularly relevant given that the CNS maintains selective communication with the peripheral immune system through structures such as the glymphatic system and meningeal lymphatic vessels, which facilitate antigen clearance and immune cross-talk between the brain and peripheral lymphoid organs. The meninges, choroid plexus and perivascular spaces are also recognized as neuroimmune hubs that coordinate immune surveillance, antigen presentation and leukocyte trafficking13. Addressing these ques- tions will be essential to determine whether EBOV persistence reflects escape from immune surveillance or an active adaptation to the CNS environment. Future organoid models incorporating cellular barriers, vascular components and peripheral immune cells will help determine how these virus–host interactions are shaped by neuroimmune com- munication and how EBOV establishes and maintains CNS reservoirs. They may also clarify whether microglia promote or restrict persistence and whether viral evolution within the CNS contributes to relapse or transmission. Collectively, these next-generation human brain models will provide a framework to investigate the mechanisms governing viral persistence in the CNS in a more physiologically relevant context. In human brain organoids, EBOV infects multiple neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia, via viral spread through budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission. Among these niches, the CNS has emerged as a particularly clinically relevant site, as studies in non- human primates have demonstrated that replication-competent EBOV can remain in the brain after clearance from the periphery, leading to fatal relapses2. Yet the mechanisms underlying EBOV persistence in the human CNS remain poorly understood, leaving key questions unanswered regarding the neural cell populations that support long- term infection and the associated host responses. Defective viral genomes are increasingly recognized as regulators of persistent infection because they can attenuate cytopathic replication while allowing for minimal levels of viral activity. By interfering with replication of full-length viral genomes, defective viral genomes have been proposed to modulate viral replication and host responses, potentially reducing cytopathic effects and contributing to persistence6. papers.title_original: Ebola virus persistence and the hidden cost of immune privilege.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how Ebola virus exploits immune-privileged environments like the central nervous system to establish persistent infection, addressing the knowledge gap in viral persistence mechanisms and the role of immune privilege in chronic infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research used human brain organoids to model the central nervous system environment, examining Ebola virus infection dynamics across multiple neural cell types including neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia.
analysis.methods: The study characterized viral replication dynamics, transmission mechanisms, viral evolution, and host immune responses in brain organoids, focusing on viral spread through budding and cell-to-cell transmission, and analysis of defective viral genomes and inflammatory mediator production.
analysis.main_results: Ebola virus infected multiple neural cell types in human brain organoids, establishing persistent infection associated with viral evolution, accumulation of defective viral genomes, and production of pro-inflammatory mediators and type I interferons by activated microglia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that immune privilege enables Ebola virus persistence by limiting pathogen clearance while allowing chronic low-level replication, with the novel finding that this persistence leads to chronic neuroinflammation and neuronal injury through viral evolution and immune activation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance strategies for Ebola virus persistence in the central nervous system, highlight the need for therapies targeting viral reservoirs in immune-privileged sites, and suggest potential neurological complications in survivors.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the use of organoid models which may not fully replicate in vivo complexity, though the study provides direct mechanistic insights into Ebola virus persistence in neural tissue.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Ebola virus establishes persistent infection in immune-privileged environments like the central nervous system using human brain organoids. The research demonstrates that Ebola virus infects multiple neural cell types (neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and microglia) through viral budding and cell-to-cell transmission. Persistent infection is associated with viral evolution, accumulation of defective viral genomes, and production of pro-inflammatory mediators and type I interferons by activated microglia, which may drive chronic neuroinflammation and neuronal injury. The findings reveal that immune privilege, while protecting essential tissues, can be exploited by pathogens as long-term reservoirs, with significant implications for understanding chronic infections and neurological complications in Ebola survivors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解 埃博拉病毒 如何利用中枢神经系统等免疫特权环境来建立持续感染,解决病毒持续机制的知识空白以及免疫特权在慢性感染中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用人脑类器官来模拟中枢神经系统环境,检查多种神经细胞类型(包括神经元、星形胶质细胞、少突胶质细胞和小胶质细胞)的 埃博拉病毒 感染动态。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究描述了脑类器官中病毒复制动力学、传播机制、病毒进化和宿主 免疫应答的特征,重点关注病毒通过出芽和细胞间传播的传播,并分析有缺陷的病毒基因组和炎症介质的产生。
elements_zh.main_results: 埃博拉病毒 感染人脑类器官中的多种神经细胞类型,建立与病毒 进化 相关的持续感染、缺陷病毒 基因组 的积累以及激活的小胶质细胞产生促炎介质和 I 型干扰素。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,免疫特权通过限制病原体清除同时允许慢性低水平复制来实现 埃博拉病毒 的持续存在,新的发现是这种持续存在通过病毒 进化 和免疫激活导致慢性神经炎症和神经元损伤。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为监测在中枢神经系统中持续存在的策略提供了信息,强调了在免疫特权部位针对病毒储存宿主的治疗的需要,并提示幸存者可能出现神经系统并发症。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管该研究提供了 埃博拉病毒 在神经组织中持久性的直接机制见解,但由于使用的类器官模型可能无法完全复制体内的复杂性,因此证据强度中等。

papers.title: Limited Durability of Improvements in Infection Prevention and Control Practices Following Reactive Interventions Leaves Healthcare Facilities Vulnerable to Ebola Virus Transmission.
papers.abstract: We assessed the impact and durability of an infection prevention and control (IPC) bundle intervention during the Kivu/Ituri Ebola virus outbreak (2018-2020). IPC scores increased, then declined 6 months postintervention (median 19/36, 30/36, and 28/36, P < .0001). Without sustained IPC, health facilities remain vulnerable to nosocomial transmission in future outbreaks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and sustainability of infection prevention and control (IPC) practices during the Kivu/Ituri Ebola virus outbreak (2018-2020). The research was motivated by the need to understand how IPC improvements could be maintained to prevent nosocomial transmission of Ebola viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted during the Kivu/Ituri Ebola virus outbreak (2018-2020) and assessed the impact of an IPC bundle intervention on health facilities. The median IPC scores were 19/36, 30/36, and 28/36 at different time points postintervention.
analysis.methods: The study used a before-and-after design to evaluate IPC scores, with assessments conducted at baseline, 6 months postintervention, and 12 months postintervention. IPC scores were measured using a standardized scoring system.
analysis.main_results: IPC scores increased after the intervention but declined 6 months postintervention (median 19/36, 30/36, and 28/36, P < .0001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that without sustained IPC efforts, health facilities remain vulnerable to future Ebola virus outbreaks. This highlights the need for ongoing monitoring and reinforcement of IPC practices.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results have important implications for the development of long-term IPC strategies in healthcare facilities to mitigate the risk of nosocomial transmission during Ebola virus outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a single time point assessment and potential for bias in self-reported IPC scores. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact and durability of an infection prevention and control (IPC) bundle intervention during the Kivu/Ituri Ebola virus outbreak (2018-2020). The research aimed to understand how IPC improvements could be sustained to prevent nosocomial transmission. IPC scores increased after the intervention but declined 6 months postintervention, indicating that without ongoing efforts, facilities remain vulnerable. The findings suggest that sustained IPC practices are essential to reduce transmission risks during future outbreaks. The study's results highlight the importance of long-term monitoring and reinforcement of IPC measures. However, the study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and a single time point assessment, which may affect the reliability of the findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估基伍/伊图里埃博拉病毒 暴发(2018-2020)期间感染预防和控制(IPC)实践的有效性和可持续性。这项研究的动机是了解如何维持 IPC 改进以防止 传播 或 埃博拉病毒 的院内感染。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在基伍/伊图里 埃博拉病毒 暴发(2018-2020 年)期间进行的,评估了 IPC 捆绑干预对卫生机构的影响。干预后不同时间点的中位 IPC 评分分别为 19/36、30/36 和 28/36。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用前后设计来评估 IPC 评分,在基线、干预后 6 个月和干预后 12 个月进行评估。IPC 分数使用标准化评分系统进行测量。
elements_zh.main_results: IPC 评分在干预后有所增加,但在干预后 6 个月有所下降(中位数 19/36、30/36 和 28/36,P < .0001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,如果没有持续的 IPC 努力,卫生机构仍然容易受到未来 埃博拉病毒 暴发 的影响。这凸显了持续监测和加强 IPC 实践的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果对于医疗机构制定长期 IPC 策略具有重要意义,以降低 埃博拉病毒 暴发 期间院内 传播 的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对单一时间点评估的依赖以及自我报告的 IPC 分数可能存在偏差而受到限制。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

analysis_zh.main_results: IPC 评分在干预后有所增加,但在干预后 6 个月有所下降(中位数 19/36、30/36 和 28/36,P < .0001)。

papers.title: Comparative Time–Space Evolution of Bundibugyo Ebolavirus Glycoprotein Across the 2007, 2012, and 2026 Outbreaks
papers.abstract: Abstract Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) is one of the recognized human-pathogenic ebolaviruses and has caused three documented outbreaks in Uganda (2007), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (2012), and the Democratic Republic of the Congo/Uganda (2026). Although complete glycoprotein (GP) sequences are available from these outbreaks, comprehensive comparative analyses integrating their temporal, geographical, and functional evolutionary characteristics remain limited. In this study, 54 complete GP amino acid sequences (676 amino acids) representing the three outbreak periods were comparatively analyzed using a unified amino acid coordinate framework. Complete sequence alignment enabled direct comparison of homologous residues across all isolates without coordinate renumbering. Core amino acid substitution sites were identified, classified according to their evolutionary behavior, and mapped onto established GP functional domains. Comparative analysis identified 21 core amino acid substitution sites distributed throughout the GP sequence. These substitutions were classified into five evolutionary patterns: fixation (n = 10), reversion (n = 4), emergence (n = 2), within-outbreak polymorphism (n = 4), and a rare variant (n = 1). Most substitutions were concentrated within the mucin-like domain (MLD) and the GP1 C-terminal region, whereas the furin cleavage site, internal fusion loop, immunosuppressive motif, and transmembrane domain remained completely conserved throughout all three outbreak periods. Temporal comparison demonstrated that GP evolution occurred primarily through amino acid substitutions rather than insertions or deletions, indicating substantial structural conservation despite continued viral evolution. These findings provide an integrated time–space overview of BDBV GP evolution across the three documented outbreaks and establish a standardized comparative framework for monitoring future genetic variation. The analytical approach presented here may facilitate genomic surveillance and support future comparative investigations of ebolavirus evolution, antigenic diversity, and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 本迪布焦埃博拉病毒(BDBV)是公认的人类致病性埃博拉病毒之一,已在乌干达(2007年)、刚果民主共和国(2012年)和刚果民主共和国/乌干达(2026年)引起三起暴发病例。尽管可以从这些 暴发 中获得完整的糖蛋白 (GP) 序列,但整合其时间、地理和功能进化特征的综合比较分析仍然有限。本研究利用统一的氨基酸坐标框架对代表三个暴发时期的54条完整GP氨基酸序列(676个氨基酸)进行了比较分析。完整的序列比对可以直接比较所有分离株的同源残基,无需重新编号坐标。核心氨基酸取代位点被确定,根据其进化行为进行分类,并映射到已建立的 GP 功能域上。比较分析确定了分布在整个 GP 序列中的 21 个核心氨基酸取代位点。这些替换被分为五种进化模式:固定(n = 10)、回复(n = 4)、出现(n = 2)、暴发 内多态性(n = 4)和罕见变异(n = 1)。大多数取代集中在粘蛋白样结构域 (MLD) 和 GP1 C 末端区域内,而弗林蛋白酶切割位点、内部融合环、免疫抑制基序和跨膜结构域在所有三个 暴发 时期保持完全保守。时间比较表明,GP 进化 主要通过氨基酸取代而不是插入或删除发生,表明尽管病毒 进化 持续存在,但仍存在大量结构保守。这些发现提供了 BDBV GP 进化 跨三个记录的 暴发 的综合时空概述,并建立了监测未来遗传变异的标准化比较框架。这里提出的分析方法可能有助于 基因组监测 并支持未来对埃博拉病毒 进化、抗原多样性和潜在治疗靶点的比较研究。

papers.title: Ebola virus exploits host lncRNA LINC01740 to enhance ATF3 and suppress antiviral immune responses 2259953
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Ebola virus (EBOV) causes a highly lethal hemorrhagic fever marked by uncontrolled cytokine release and impaired antiviral defense. EBOV primarily infects human macrophages, where uncontrolled replication reprograms host transcription and fuels hyperinflammation. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), potent regulators of transcription and immunity, remain largely unexplored in EBOV pathogenesis. We identified EBOV-induced lncRNAs co-regulated with transcription factors (TFs) in primary human macrophages, revealing a novel mechanism by which EBOV rewires host gene expression to promote immune suppression and persistence Methods Using the highly virulent EBOV (Mayinga variant), we infected primary human macrophages from nine donors. We compared protein-coding and lncRNA transcriptomes of EBOV-infected vs. MOCK-infected macrophages at 24- and 48-hours post-infection. Differentially expressed lncRNAs were correlated with adjacent protein-coding genes to infer cis-regulatory relationships. Functional validation used antisense oligonucleotides, CRISPR interference (CRISPRi), and inducible CRISPR—Cas13d knockdown, followed by qPCR, RNA-seq, and Western blotting Results EBOV infection triggered extensive remodeling of macrophage transcriptome. LINC01740 was strongly induced and tightly co-expressed with its neighboring gene, ATF3, a stress-responsive transcription factor known to repress antiviral signaling. LINC01740 knockdown reduced ATF3 expression in macrophages. ATF3 inhibition restored interferon-beta production, enhanced innate immune activation, and induced strong antiviral responses in EBOV-infected macrophages. Our data show that ATF3 impairs IFN-I responses in macrophages, contributing to immune paralysis Conclusion Our data revealed LINC01740 as a novel host lncRNA co-opted by EBOV to enhance ATF3 and suppress antiviral responses. Here we show a novel LINC01740—ATF3—IFN-I regulatory axis driving immune evasion and viral persistence, highlighting lncRNAs as potential antiviral therapeutic targets Funding Source n/a Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Ebola virus (EBOV) exploits the host long non-coding RNA LINC01740 to enhance ATF3 expression and suppress antiviral immune responses. papers.title: Ring and community vaccination for Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak response: a stochastic network modelling study
papers.abstract: Background: Vaccination with rVSV-ZEBOV is highly effective against Zaire ebolavirus, but protection against Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) is unproven. We evaluated the relative population impact and dose efficiency of a partially cross-protective hypothetical vaccine under operationally realistic constraints during a BDBV outbreak. Methods: We developed a stochastic transmission model on a two-layer household-community contact network calibrated to 2026 Democratic Republic of the Congo BDBV outbreak data. Time-varying effective reproduction numbers were estimated using a Bayesian renewal model. We evaluated case detection, isolation, contact tracing, reactive ring vaccination, and community vaccination (20-80% coverage). Base-case vaccine efficacy was 45% and included post-exposure protection against disease and mortality. Primary outcomes were mortality and incidence reductions, total doses, and dose efficiency (doses per death averted) over 90 days, evaluated in a probabilistic sensitivity analysis with 10,000 matched stochastic replicates per strategy. Results: Compared with base operations alone (30% detection, 30% tracing), enhanced operations alone (70% detection, 80% tracing) reduced expected mortality by 81.9% (95% UI 72.3-88.8). Reactive Ring 2 vaccination under base operations reduced mortality by 7.8% (4.7-10.9), requiring 89.5 doses per death averted. Added to enhanced operations, Ring 2 vaccination reduced mortality by 82.5% overall (73.0-88.9), an incremental benefit of 2.7% (0.9-4.9) beyond enhanced operations alone. Community vaccination at 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% coverage reduced mortality by 44.4% (33.9-51.8), 67.9% (56.7-75.6), 80.4% (70.8-85.9), and 87.2% (79.6-91.3), requiring 40.3 to 80.9 doses per death averted. Interpretation: Strengthened case finding, contact tracing, and isolation averted most deaths even without vaccination. Once these operations were strong, reactive ring vaccination added little further benefit, whereas rapid community vaccination produced the largest reductions in simulated scenarios but required substantially more doses. A partially protective BDBV vaccine's population-level value will depend principally on rapid, broad delivery.

papers.title: Cost-effectiveness of geographically targeted versus ring vaccination campaigns in response to an outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease caused by Orthoebolavirus zairense
papers.abstract: BackgroundWHO recommends ring vaccination (RV) of Ebola virus disease (EVD) case contact chains to contain outbreaks of Orthoebolavirus zairense. However, this strategy can falter in remote or conflict-affected settings where effective contact tracing is challenging. Targeted geographic vaccination (TGV) - immunising everyone near an EVD cases location without requiring contact tracing - has been implemented as an alternative. We compare the epidemiological impact and cost-effectiveness of TGV versus RV under diverse outbreak scenarios. MethodsWe extended a spatially-explicit individual-based stochastic EVD transmission model calibrated to outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We simulated outbreaks varying both epidemiological and operational parameters. We evaluated vaccination strategies on total cases, deaths, epidemic duration, vaccine doses used, and incremental net monetary benefit (INMB). ResultsNo single strategy dominates in all scenarios. For better overall response performance, RV results in substantially fewer cases and deaths than TGV (approximately 20% fewer cases), requires fewer doses, and has higher INMB more frequently. Under pessimistic response assumptions, TGV slightly outperforms RV by preventing more infections, curbing the largest outbreaks, and using fewer doses, although the INMBs are similar between strategies. InterpretationDifferent operational contexts recommend different vaccination strategies. Overall, surveillance, contact tracing, and isolation have the most impact on Orthoebolavirus zairense outbreak control. Depending on response effectiveness, the preferred strategy for adding vaccination varies. Backed by effective case detection and management, RV appears the better approach. Under severe response constraints, TGV can be more effective.

papers.title_zh: 针对由扎伊伦斯正博拉病毒引起的 暴发 或 埃博拉病毒病 的地理定向活动与 环形疫苗接种 活动的成本效益
papers.source_body_en: BackgroundWHO recommends ring vaccination (RV) of Ebola virus disease (EVD) case contact chains to contain outbreaks of Orthoebolavirus zairense. However, this strategy can falter in remote or conflict-affected settings where effective contact tracing is challenging. Targeted geographic vaccination (TGV) - immunising everyone near an EVD cases location without requiring contact tracing - has been implemented as an alternative. We compare the epidemiological impact and cost-effectiveness of TGV versus RV under diverse outbreak scenarios. MethodsWe extended a spatially-explicit individual-based stochastic EVD transmission model calibrated to outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We simulated outbreaks varying both epidemiological and operational parameters. We evaluated vaccination strategies on total cases, deaths, epidemic duration, vaccine doses used, and incremental net monetary benefit (INMB). ResultsNo single strategy dominates in all scenarios. For better overall response performance, RV results in substantially fewer cases and deaths than TGV (approximately 20% fewer cases), requires fewer doses, and has higher INMB more frequently. Under pessimistic response assumptions, TGV slightly outperforms RV by preventing more infections, curbing the largest outbreaks, and using fewer doses, although the INMBs are similar between strategies. InterpretationDifferent operational contexts recommend different vaccination strategies. Overall, surveillance, contact tracing, and isolation have the most impact on Orthoebolavirus zairense outbreak control. Depending on response effectiveness, the preferred strategy for adding vaccination varies. Backed by effective case detection and management, RV appears the better approach. Under severe response constraints, TGV can be more effective.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景世界卫生组织建议 埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 病例接触链的 环形疫苗接种 (RV) 包含扎伊尔塞正埃博拉病毒 暴发。然而,在偏远地区或受冲突影响的环境中,有效的接触者追踪具有挑战性,这一策略可能会动摇。有针对性的地理 疫苗接种 (TGV)——对埃博拉病毒病病例地点附近的每个人进行免疫接种,无需追踪接触者——已作为替代方案实施。我们比较了不同 暴发 情景下 TGV 与 RV 的流行病学影响和成本效益。方法我们扩展了一个基于空间显式个体的随机 EVD 传播 模型,该模型在刚果民主共和国校准为 暴发。我们模拟了改变流行病学和操作参数的 暴发。我们评估了 疫苗接种 策略的总病例数、死亡人数、流行持续时间、使用的 疫苗 剂量和增量净货币效益 (INMB)。结果没有一种策略能够在所有情况下占主导地位。为了获得更好的总体反应表现,RV 导致的病例和死亡人数比 TGV 少得多(大约减少 20% 的病例),需要的剂量更少,并且 INMB 更高。在悲观反应假设下,TGV 通过预防更多感染、抑制最大 暴发 和使用更少剂量而略微优于 RV,尽管策略之间的 INMB 相似。解读不同的运营环境推荐不同的疫苗接种策略。总体而言,监测、接触者追踪和隔离对扎伊尔塞正博拉病毒 暴发 控制影响最大。根据响应有效性,添加 疫苗接种 的首选策略会有所不同。在有效的病例检测和管理的支持下,RV 似乎是更好的方法。在严重的响应限制下,TGV 可以更加有效。

papers.title: Estimating the effectiveness of syndromic screening at airports for Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease
papers.abstract: We used a stochastic simulation model to estimate the effectiveness of exit and/or entry syndromic screening at airports for Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease (BVD). For a 12-hour international flight from DRC or Uganda at 86% screening sensitivity, approximately 73% of infected people presenting for travel would evade combined exit and entry screening (95% CrI: 68-77%). Among those who successfully boarded, approximately 92% would arrive without detection (95% CrI: 90-94%). This high undetected fraction reflects the relative durations of the incubation period (approximately 7.7 days; Wamala et al. 20101) and the onset-to-severe-disease interval (approximately 4 days; Funk & Abbott 20262): most infected travellers board before symptom onset and are undetectable by any syndromic screen, whilst those who are symptomatic progress rapidly to illness severe enough to preclude travel. Because the proportion of confirmed cases presenting without fever is itself uncertain, we also report a conservative scenario in which all confirmed cases are febrile (0% asymptomatic-equivalent), under which the undetected fraction remains substantial at approximately 64% (95% CrI: 57-70%). This is compounded during active epidemic growth, when recently exposed (and therefore pre-symptomatic) cases are overrepresented among travellers. Syndromic airport screening offers limited protection against BVD spread via air travel, and should be complemented by outbreak control at source, strengthened clinical surveillance in receiving countries with high travel connectivity to affected areas, and post-departure self-monitoring guidance for travellers from affected regions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to estimate the effectiveness of syndromic screening at airports for Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease (BVD) to address the public health challenge of preventing its spread via international air travel.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research used a stochastic simulation model to evaluate exit and/or entry syndromic screening for BVD on a 12-hour international flight from DRC or Uganda.
analysis.methods: The study employed a stochastic simulation model to estimate screening effectiveness, incorporating parameters such as incubation period (approximately 7.7 days) and onset-to-severe-disease interval (approximately 4 days), and analyzed scenarios with varying proportions of febrile cases.
analysis.main_results: At 86% screening sensitivity, approximately 73% of infected travelers would evade combined exit and entry screening (95% CrI: 68-77%), and among those who boarded, approximately 92% would arrive undetected (95% CrI: 90-94%). Even in a conservative scenario where all confirmed cases are febrile, the undetected fraction remained substantial at approximately 64% (95% CrI: 57-70%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high undetected fraction as reflecting the relative durations of the incubation period and onset-to-severe-disease interval, noting that most infected travelers board before symptom onset, while symptomatic individuals progress too rapidly to travel. The novelty lies in quantifying the limitations of syndromic screening for BVD under realistic epidemic conditions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that syndromic airport screening offers limited protection against BVD spread via air travel and should be complemented by outbreak control at source, strengthened clinical surveillance in high-connectivity receiving countries, and post-departure self-monitoring guidance for travelers from affected regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on a simulation model with assumptions about incubation periods and symptom presentation, and the proportion of confirmed cases without fever remains uncertain, which could affect the generalizability of the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study used a stochastic simulation model to estimate the effectiveness of syndromic screening at airports for Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease (BVD). The results showed that at 86% screening sensitivity, approximately 73% of infected travelers would evade combined exit and entry screening, and 92% of those who boarded would arrive undetected. Even in a conservative scenario where all confirmed cases are febrile, the undetected fraction remained substantial at 64%. The authors attribute this to the longer incubation period compared to the rapid progression to severe illness, meaning most infected travelers are asymptomatic at boarding. The findings indicate that syndromic screening alone offers limited protection and should be complemented by outbreak control at source, enhanced surveillance in high-connectivity countries, and traveler self-monitoring guidance.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估机场对本迪布焦埃博拉病毒病(BVD)进行症状筛查的有效性,以应对防止其通过国际航空旅行传播的公共卫生挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用随机模拟模型来评估从刚果民主共和国或乌干达起飞的 12 小时国际航班上的 BVD 出境和/或入境综合征筛查。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用随机模拟模型来估计筛查有效性,结合潜伏期(约7.7天)和发病到重症间隔(约4天)等参数,并分析了不同比例发热病例的情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 在筛查敏感度为 86% 的情况下,大约 73% 的受感染旅客将逃避出境和入境联合筛查(95% CrI:68-77%),而在登机的旅客中,大约 92% 的人抵达时不会被发现(95% CrI:90-94%)。即使在所有确诊病例均发热的保守情况下,未检测到的比例仍然很高,约为 64%(95% CrI:57-70%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将未发现的高比例解释为反映了潜伏期和发病到严重疾病间隔的相对持续时间,并指出大多数受感染的旅行者在症状出现之前登机,而有症状的个体进展太快而无法旅行。新颖之处在于量化现实流行条件下 BVD 综合征筛查的局限性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,综合症机场筛查对通过航空旅行传播 BVD 的保护有限,应辅之以 暴发 源头控制、在高连通性接收国加强临床 监测 以及对来自受影响地区的旅行者的出发后自我监测指导。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究依赖于对潜伏期和症状表现进行假设的模拟模型,并且不发烧的确诊病例的比例仍然不确定,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to estimate the effectiveness of syndromic screening at airports for Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease (BVD) to address the public health challenge of preventing its spread via international air travel.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The research used a stochastic simulation model to evaluate exit and/or entry syndromic screening for BVD on a 12-hour international flight from DRC or Uganda.
analysis_en.methods: The study employed a stochastic simulation model to estimate screening effectiveness, incorporating parameters such as incubation period (approximately 7.7 days) and onset-to-severe-disease interval (approximately 4 days), and analyzed scenarios with varying proportions of febrile cases.
analysis_en.main_results: At 86% screening sensitivity, approximately 73% of infected travelers would evade combined exit and entry screening (95% CrI: 68-77%), and among those who boarded, approximately 92% would arrive undetected (95% CrI: 90-94%). Even in a conservative scenario where all confirmed cases are febrile, the undetected fraction remained substantial at approximately 64% (95% CrI: 57-70%).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high undetected fraction as reflecting the relative durations of the incubation period and onset-to-severe-disease interval, noting that most infected travelers board before symptom onset, while symptomatic individuals progress too rapidly to travel. The novelty lies in quantifying the limitations of syndromic screening for BVD under realistic epidemic conditions.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that syndromic airport screening offers limited protection against BVD spread via air travel and should be complemented by outbreak control at source, strengthened clinical surveillance in high-connectivity receiving countries, and post-departure self-monitoring guidance for travelers from affected regions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on a simulation model with assumptions about incubation periods and symptom presentation, and the proportion of confirmed cases without fever remains uncertain, which could affect the generalizability of the results.

papers.title_zh: 评估机场针对本迪布焦埃博拉病毒病进行症状筛查的有效性
papers.source_body_en: We used a stochastic simulation model to estimate the effectiveness of exit and/or entry syndromic screening at airports for Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease (BVD). For a 12-hour international flight from DRC or Uganda at 86% screening sensitivity, approximately 73% of infected people presenting for travel would evade combined exit and entry screening (95% CrI: 68-77%). Among those who successfully boarded, approximately 92% would arrive without detection (95% CrI: 90-94%). This high undetected fraction reflects the relative durations of the incubation period (approximately 7.7 days; Wamala et al. 20101) and the onset-to-severe-disease interval (approximately 4 days; Funk & Abbott 20262): most infected travellers board before symptom onset and are undetectable by any syndromic screen, whilst those who are symptomatic progress rapidly to illness severe enough to preclude travel. Because the proportion of confirmed cases presenting without fever is itself uncertain, we also report a conservative scenario in which all confirmed cases are febrile (0% asymptomatic-equivalent), under which the undetected fraction remains substantial at approximately 64% (95% CrI: 57-70%). This is compounded during active epidemic growth, when recently exposed (and therefore pre-symptomatic) cases are overrepresented among travellers. Syndromic airport screening offers limited protection against BVD spread via air travel, and should be complemented by outbreak control at source, strengthened clinical surveillance in receiving countries with high travel connectivity to affected areas, and post-departure self-monitoring guidance for travellers from affected regions.

papers.title: "Blame the bats again": YouTube reactions to the 2026 Ebola public health emergency reveal mistrust, misinformation, and geopolitical anxiety
papers.abstract: Abstract The World Health Organization declared the 2026 outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Public engagement on video-sharing platforms such as YouTube offers insight into public perceptions during such crises, particularly in the affected region, yet these reactions remain largely uncharacterised. We analysed public discourse and sentiment surrounding the outbreak, focusing on thematic trends in YouTube comments, using a qualitative synthesis that combined thematic content analysis with topic modelling. Videos were identified through the YouTube Data application programming interface, which returned 50 videos each for the search terms “Ebola” and “Ebola virus disease.” After removing duplicates and excluding videos published before the 17 May 2026 emergency declaration, the 10 most-viewed videos were retained. From 4,457 extracted comments, 4,087 were analysed using Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modelling, complemented by a lexicon-based sentiment analysis. Five themes emerged: geopolitical and cultural context; public figures, conspiracy theories, and misinformation; disease spread and transmission; public health measures and preparedness; and religious and spiritual interpretation. Discourse was strongly shaped by border concerns, mistrust of institutions, global aid politics, and comparisons with COVID-19, and sentiment was split near-evenly between fear and trust. Effective health communication during this outbreak must therefore address not only the scientific and medical dimensions of the emergency but also its geopolitical, cultural, and religious dimensions, while countering misinformation and building public trust.

papers.title: What the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda reveals about epidemic preparedness in West Africa
papers.abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda has exposed critical vulnerabilities in epidemic preparedness despite substantial investments in health security following previous Ebola epidemics. Unlike outbreaks caused by the Zaire strain of Ebola virus, no licensed vaccines, approved therapeutics, or widely available rapid diagnostics currently exist for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease. Consequently, affected countries have had to respond to an active outbreak while simultaneously generating evidence to guide control measures. In this perspective, we argue that while substantial global frameworks exist, including CEPI’s 100 Days Mission, WHO’s R&D Blueprint, and Africa CDC’s initiatives, the operationalization of research readiness systems at regional and national levels remains an area requiring continued investment. Drawing on experiences from West Africa following the 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic, we hypothesize that the absence of pre-approved protocols, standing ethics mechanisms, clinical trial networks, and emergency financing arrangements may represent a more critical gap than the absence of medical countermeasures themselves. We wish to clarify that our argument is not that research is absent during outbreaks; indeed, significant research efforts have been mounted during the Bundibugyo outbreak, but rather that the speed with which research can be initiated is constrained by the absence of pre-positioned systems. We reflect on progress in surveillance, laboratory systems, and regional coordination while highlighting persistent weaknesses in regulatory harmonization, emergency financing, cross-border collaboration, and community engagement. We discuss how the Lassa Fever Coalition in West Africa and global initiatives such as CEPI’s 100 Days Mission provide useful frameworks for strengthening preparedness before crises occur. We contend that epidemic preparedness should be viewed not only as a technical exercise but also as a political, institutional, and social investment and that research readiness requires systematic attention as a core component of health security. Sustained commitment to research readiness, financing, and regional collaboration will be essential if West Africa is to respond effectively to future epidemic threats.

papers.abstract_zh: 2026年刚果民主共和国(DRC)和乌干达的邦迪布焦埃博拉病毒暴发暴露了疫情准备方面的关键脆弱性,尽管在前几次埃博拉疫情后已对卫生安全进行了大量投资。与由埃博拉病毒埃博拉病毒的扎伊尔株引起的暴发不同,目前尚无针对邦迪布焦埃博拉病毒埃博拉病毒病的许可疫苗、获批的治疗药物或广泛可用的快速诊断方法。因此,受影响国家不得不在同时生成指导控制措施的循证证据的同时应对活跃的暴发。在本观点文章中,我们认为,尽管存在大量全球框架,包括CEPI的100天任务、世卫组织的研发蓝图和非洲疾控中心的倡议,但在区域和国家层面实施研究准备系统仍是需要持续投入的领域。借鉴2014-2016年埃博拉疫情后西非的经验,我们假设,预先批准的方案、常设伦理机制、临床试验网络和紧急融资安排的缺失可能比医疗对策本身的缺失代表更关键的差距。我们希望澄清,我们的论点并非认为在暴发期间研究缺失;事实上,在邦迪布焦埃博拉病毒暴发期间已开展了大量研究工作,而是研究启动的速度因预先部署系统的缺失而受到限制。我们反思了监测、实验室系统和区域协调方面的进展,同时强调了在监管协调、紧急融资、跨境合作和社区参与方面存在的持续弱点。我们讨论了西非的拉沙热联盟和全球性倡议(如CEPI的100天任务)如何为危机前加强准备工作提供了有用的框架。我们认为,疫情准备不仅应被视为技术性工作,还应被视为政治、制度和社会投资,而研究准备需要作为卫生安全的核心组成部分得到系统性关注。如果西非要有效应对未来的疫情威胁,对研究准备、融资和区域合作的持续承诺将是必不可少的。

papers.title: Fever Temperatures Differentially Alter Ebola-Antibody Functionality Depending on Affinity Maturation 2306819
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction In 2013-16, Western Africa experienced the largest known outbreak of the highly lethal virus, Ebolavirus (EBOV) and ongoing sporadic outbreaks have occurred since. EBOV is the causative agent of EBOV hemorrhagic fever, characterized by a high-grade fever. Antibody responses to EBOV have been correlated with protection against EBOV disease. However, it is unclear how antibody functions result in protection from repeat exposure. Understanding antibody-mediated mechanisms of protection against Ebola infection is critical to maximize long-term protection against infection. Methods We utilize a systems serology approach to analyze a cohort of 60 survivors of the 2013-16 Ebola epidemic in Guinea and 81 individuals of pygmy ancestry in the Republic of Congo who did not have documented EBOV infection, but do experience frequent zoonotic exposures to characterize the impact of fever conditions on affinity matured EBOV-directed antibody responses. Antibody binding and cellular activation were measured at both physiologic (37C) and high grade fever (40C) temperatures. Results We show that neutralization of EBOV is impaired under fever temperatures, both for affinity-matured and non-specific antibody responses. In contrast, effector-mediated functions, particularly against the EBOV soluble glycoprotein (sGP, a signature previously linked to enhanced protection in animal vaccine challenge models), are enhanced at febrile temperatures. This temperature-sensitive enhancement of effector function correlates with full length GP and sGP-directed IgG subclasses, IgA, FcγR-binding- and FcαR-binding antibodies, demonstrating a highly associated network of humoral features that are maintained during periods of febrile temperatures. Conclusion Collectively, our findings suggest that although neutralization plays a key role in surveillance in a non-fever state, fever modulates affinity-matured antibody responses to the hemorrhagic fever-inducing EBOV, moving antibody profiles to a pro-effector function phenotype. Funding Source NIH NIAID U19 AI135995 Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

papers.title_zh: 发烧温度会根据亲和力成熟程度不同地改变埃博拉抗体功能 2306819
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction In 2013-16, Western Africa experienced the largest known outbreak of the highly lethal virus, Ebolavirus (EBOV) and ongoing sporadic outbreaks have occurred since. EBOV is the causative agent of EBOV hemorrhagic fever, characterized by a high-grade fever. Antibody responses to EBOV have been correlated with protection against EBOV disease. However, it is unclear how antibody functions result in protection from repeat exposure. Understanding antibody-mediated mechanisms of protection against Ebola infection is critical to maximize long-term protection against infection. Methods We utilize a systems serology approach to analyze a cohort of 60 survivors of the 2013-16 Ebola epidemic in Guinea and 81 individuals of pygmy ancestry in the Republic of Congo who did not have documented EBOV infection, but do experience frequent zoonotic exposures to characterize the impact of fever conditions on affinity matured EBOV-directed antibody responses. Antibody binding and cellular activation were measured at both physiologic (37C) and high grade fever (40C) temperatures. Results We show that neutralization of EBOV is impaired under fever temperatures, both for affinity-matured and non-specific antibody responses. In contrast, effector-mediated functions, particularly against the EBOV soluble glycoprotein (sGP, a signature previously linked to enhanced protection in animal vaccine challenge models), are enhanced at febrile temperatures. This temperature-sensitive enhancement of effector function correlates with full length GP and sGP-directed IgG subclasses, IgA, FcγR-binding- and FcαR-binding antibodies, demonstrating a highly associated network of humoral features that are maintained during periods of febrile temperatures. Conclusion Collectively, our findings suggest that although neutralization plays a key role in surveillance in a non-fever state, fever modulates affinity-matured antibody responses to the hemorrhagic fever-inducing EBOV, moving antibody profiles to a pro-effector function phenotype. Funding Source NIH NIAID U19 AI135995 Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 介绍 2013-16 年,西非经历了已知最大规模的高致命病毒埃博拉病毒(EBOV)暴发,此后又发生了持续的散发性 暴发。埃博拉病毒是埃博拉病毒出血热的病原体,其特征是高烧。对 EBOV 的抗体反应与预防 EBOV 疾病相关。然而,尚不清楚抗体的功能如何防止重复暴露。了解抗体介导的埃博拉感染保护机制对于最大限度地长期预防感染至关重要。方法 我们利用系统 血清学 方法对 2013-16 几内亚埃博拉疫情的 60 名幸存者和刚果共和国的 81 名侏儒血统个体进行 队列研究 分析,这些幸存者没有记录到埃博拉病毒感染,但确实经历过频繁的人畜共患病暴露,以表征发烧状况对亲和力成熟的埃博拉病毒导向抗体反应的影响。在生理温度 (37°C) 和高烧温度 (40°C) 下测量抗体结合和细胞激活。结果我们发现,对于亲和力成熟的抗体反应和非特异性抗体反应,在发烧温度下,EBOV 的中和作用都会受到损害。相比之下,效应子介导的功能,特别是针对 EBOV 可溶性糖蛋白(sGP,以前与动物 疫苗 攻击模型中增强保护有关的特征),在发热时会增强。这种效应功能的温度敏感性增强与全长 GP 和 sGP 导向的 IgG 亚类、IgA、FcγR 结合抗体和 FcαR 结合抗体相关,证明了在发热期间维持的高度相关的体液特征网络。结论 总的来说,我们的研究结果表明,虽然中和在非发烧状态下的 监测 中发挥关键作用,但发烧调节亲和力成熟的抗体对引起出血热的 EBOV 的反应,将抗体谱转变为前效应子功能表型。资金来源 NIH NIAID U19 AI135995 主题类别 病毒免疫学 (VIR)

papers.title: It’s not just virology: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda demands a wider public health response
papers.abstract: The current outbreak of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus (species Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda is much more than another infectious disease emergency. It reminds us that epidemics come not only from biological pathogens but also from social inequities, environmental disruption, fragile health systems, and persistent armed conflict. While Ebola captures headlines because of its fear-provoking symptoms and high mortality, the conditions that allow it to spread receive far less attention.

papers.abstract_zh: 当前刚果民主共和国(DRC)和乌干达由本迪布焦病毒(本迪布焦正埃博拉病毒属)引起的埃博拉疫情不仅仅是另一种传染病紧急情况。它提醒我们,流行病不仅来自生物病原体,还来自社会不平等、环境破坏、脆弱的卫生系统和持续的武装冲突。虽然埃博拉病毒因其令人恐惧的症状和高 死亡率 而成为头条新闻,但导致其传播的条件却很少受到关注。
